summary: Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked today, so this report rests on verified Hacker News comment threads. Strongest themes: people leaving 1Password over the dropped offline vault, newsrooms warning photographers off Photoshop's AI features, GitHub outages pushing people toward paid managed Forgejo, job seekers filtered out by software before a human sees them, and Windows 11's Settings app replacing the Control Panel.

ideas.title: Offline-first password vault with bring-your-own sync
ideas.oneLiner: A 1Password-7-style local vault that syncs through storage you pick (iCloud, Dropbox, Syncthing) and imports old vaults without losing dates or choking on bad fields.
ideas.problem: After the 1Password incident disclosure, long-time users say they want a local-only vault but can't get one with good UX. 1Password dropped offline vaults, KeePass-style tools lack polished sync/sharing, and Vaultwarden imports lose creation dates and fail entirely if one item has a bad field.
ideas.targetUsers: Security-conscious individuals, families and small teams who distrust cloud-hosted vaults but won't give up multi-device sync and passkeys.
ideas.monetization: One-time licence per platform (around $29–49) or a $20–30/year sync-and-updates tier. Commenters say they'd still pay a subscription for a local-only option.
mvp: Encrypted local vault file with a modern native UI
Optional sync through the user's own folder (iCloud, Dropbox, Syncthing)
Tolerant importer for 1Password .1pux and Bitwarden exports that keeps original created/modified dates and skips or flags oversized fields instead of failing
TOTP and passkey storage
Browser autofill extension that talks to the local app
Family sharing via exported shared vaults

competitors.name: KeePassXC
competitors.gap: Trusted and local, but commenters note sync and sharing across Linux, Mac, iPhone and a partner is manual, and the UX is not 1Password-grade.

competitors.name: Vaultwarden / Bitwarden
competitors.gap: Self-hostable, but one user reports import resets creation dates and fails the whole import on a single bad field, and dislikes JavaScript-based clients.

competitors.name: 1Password
competitors.gap: Dropped offline vaults and moved to a cloud-first client; users cite this as the reason they're leaving.

sources.title: 1Password Security Incident

sources.title: 1Password Security Incident

sources.title: 1Password Security Incident

ideas.title: AI-use auditor for photos and PSDs
ideas.oneLiner: Drop in a photo or layered file and get a plain report of whether generative AI touched it, before it goes to an editor or social platform.
ideas.problem: The New York Times told photographers not to update Photoshop because generative features can be used by accident. Commenters point out that provenance standards only identify the problem after the fact, and that even minor AI edits can earn a platform's AI-generated tag.
ideas.targetUsers: Freelance and staff photojournalists, photo editors, and brand teams that publish on Instagram or Facebook.
ideas.monetization: Free single-file check; $9–19/month for batch scanning and PDF audit reports, plus a team plan for newsrooms.
mvp: Read C2PA/Content Credentials and XMP history to flag generative-fill or AI-generated assets
Scan PSD layers for generative layers
Batch-check a folder before submission
Exportable pass/fail report for the editor
Offline processing so unpublished photos stay on the machine

competitors.name: Content Credentials Verify
competitors.gap: Shows credentials after the fact for one image at a time; commenters note it does not stop accidental AI use or give a batch pre-submission check.

competitors.name: Adobe AI-off settings
competitors.gap: Some tools have toggles, but a commenter says photographers still hit AI features inadvertently because they are not clearly distinguished from traditional tools.

sources.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
sources.quote: The core problem which the Times has identified here is that photographers are using GenAI tools in Photoshop inadvertently because they are not clearly distinguished from traditional editing tools.

sources.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
sources.quote: Adobe and others can plausibly distribute AI-free builds or just have a big AI-off switch that can disable AI-tainting features for a work session to prevent inadvertent use.

sources.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
sources.quote: I work in the creative tools space. This is one of the biggest issues right now.

sources.title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
sources.quote: it's using newer Photoshop versions that potentially uses generative AI without you knowing (which is a risk for journalists publishing photos).

ideas.title: Managed Forgejo hosting with GitHub mirroring
ideas.oneLiner: Hosted, patched Forgejo with CI runners and common integrations preconfigured, plus a one-click two-way mirror to GitHub.
ideas.problem: During another GitHub degradation, developers said it is frustrating and interferes with work, and one asked outright for a company that hosts Forgejo for them. Self-hosting worries them (CVEs), and users of Gitea/Forgejo say missing integrations make it painful at work.
ideas.targetUsers: Small dev teams and indie developers who want a GitHub fallback or exit without running their own server.
ideas.monetization: Per-seat or per-repo-bundle subscription ($4–8/user/month) with a free tier for small public projects.
mvp: One-click provisioned, auto-patched Forgejo instance
Push mirror to and from GitHub
Hosted CI runners compatible with Actions workflows
Preconfigured webhooks for common security, review and agent tools
Daily backups and export
Per-agent accounts included at no extra seat cost

competitors.name: Codeberg
competitors.gap: Free and non-commercial; a commenter says it has a weekly maintenance window of up to 8 hours and would not host every project.

competitors.name: Self-hosted Forgejo
competitors.gap: Fast per commenters, but they must patch it and wire up integrations themselves.

competitors.name: GitLab
competitors.gap: Hosted alternative, but heavier and not the lightweight GitHub-like workflow these commenters want.

sources.title: Investigating degraded experiences across GitHub products
sources.quote: Host Forgejo for me or build your own thing (Cloudflare Artifacts looks pretty promising). For my own things I self host Forgejo, but considering the fun CVE's floating around lately I'd rather pay someone to host this for me.

sources.title: Investigating degraded experiences across GitHub products

sources.title: Investigating degraded experiences across GitHub products

ideas.title: Recruiter-search and ATS visibility checker
ideas.oneLiner: Paste your resume or LinkedIn profile and see which recruiter Boolean searches and ATS rankings you would appear in, with fixes.
ideas.problem: Job seekers say software screens them out before a human looks: recruiters run LinkedIn Boolean searches that bucket a profile as backend instead of full-stack, and ATS ranking penalises resume gaps.
ideas.targetUsers: Laid-off and long-term-searching engineers and other professionals, especially with gaps or hybrid profiles.
ideas.monetization: Free scan; $9–15/month for unlimited scans, role-targeted rewrite suggestions, and gap-explanation templates.
mvp: Paste resume or profile text
Generate typical recruiter Boolean queries for a target role and show hit/miss
Flag gap and keyword issues an ATS may rank down
Suggest wording to move the profile into the right bucket
Side-by-side before/after score

competitors.name: Jobscan
competitors.gap: Compares a resume to one job description; does not simulate the recruiter-side Boolean searches commenters describe.

competitors.name: Teal
competitors.gap: Resume and tracking suite; not focused on whether you surface in recruiter searches.

sources.title: Ask HN: I have been unemployed for 2y. 15 years of experience, US. What to do?
sources.quote: one recruiter even said that I didn't got a screening before, because my profile is drawed against backend profile and not fullstack, because they do linkedin boolean searches.

sources.title: Ask HN: I have been unemployed for 2y. 15 years of experience, US. What to do?
sources.quote: Resume gaps matter to an ATS if you are looking for a job now, because your competition (either real - people laid off recently - or fake - there’s boatloads of resume fraud in the last few years) doesn’t have those gaps and the software will rank them higher.

sources.title: Ask HN: I have been unemployed for 2y. 15 years of experience, US. What to do?
sources.quote: my traditional job sources have decayed in quality, and that it's possible to spend all day every day applying for positions I'm qualified for but wouldn't enjoy at companies that will never call me back.

ideas.title: Classic Control Panel finder for Windows 11
ideas.oneLiner: A searchable launcher that maps every Windows 11 setting, including buried legacy Control Panel and policy settings, to one-click shortcuts with plain explanations.
ideas.problem: Users say the Windows 11 Settings app hides options, has confusing labels, and leaves many settings only in the old Control Panel, forcing them into PowerShell, Group Policy or the registry.
ideas.targetUsers: Power users, IT admins and helpers of non-technical relatives on Windows 10/11.
ideas.monetization: Free for personal use; $10 one-time Pro licence for exporting presets and admin features.
mvp: Index of Settings pages plus legacy Control Panel applets
Fuzzy search by task wording
Plain-language descriptions and the registry/policy key each toggle changes
Pin favourite settings to the Start menu
Export a settings checklist for family or IT

competitors.name: Winaero Tweaker
competitors.gap: Powerful but organised by technical category, not task search with explanations.

competitors.name: ExplorerPatcher
competitors.gap: Restores old shell pieces but does not make buried settings discoverable or explain them.
